records.description: A long-running Copenhagen directory listing describes a public restroom on the approach to Langelinie, near the historic Kastellet fort. The original contributor suggested weekday afternoons, roughly 16:00–17:30, but those times are undated and not an established current pattern. The city lists toilets around both Langelinie and Langeliniebro, and the evidence does not establish which one the cruising account meant. The newest readable comment on the individual page is from September 2025; a June 2026 city-page message merely proposes a visit. If you are walking around Kastellet, bear in mind public toilets can close seasonally or in the evening. There is no confirmed present-day gathering point, visitor profile or reliable 2026 firsthand encounter to support advertising this as an active spot.
records.opening_notes: Municipal public-toilet seasonal hours apply; archived afternoon recommendation unverified.

records.description: The ornamental grounds around the Zappeion exhibition hall in central Athens have featured in cruising directories for years. The older description points to the fountain south of the main building and paths through nearby planting, with dusk as a suggested visiting period. More recent accounts are less straightforward: a February 2026 visitor said the gardens were empty, while a June commenter described the men they had seen without reporting an encounter. Other June posts are simply plans to visit. This is a shared landscape beside the National Garden, which has its own separate gates and sunset closure. Don't mix the two parks together or assume the Zappeion grounds permit entry everywhere throughout the night. There isn't enough contemporary evidence to promise a crowd, age range or reliable best time.
records.address: Zappeion grounds, near the fountain south of Zappeion Megaron, Athens
records.tags: Gardens, City Park, Dusk, Historical Reports
records.opening_notes: Old directory suggests dusk; not corroborated by successful 2026 visitor reports.

records.description: Plateía Daváki is a neighbourhood square in Kallithea, south-west of central Athens. An old directory talks about a toilet near the square's main entrance, describes visitors of different ages and suggests midday through evening before park closure. Those details aren't backed by a contemporary firsthand report, and the exact toilet layout and operating hours are not independently confirmed. A March 2026 user asked to meet somebody, but didn't describe having been there; the individual listing itself has almost no meaningful recent commentary. The square is public and local records have referred to municipal security patrols, so it should not be described as a private or unrestricted venue. Unless a more recent visit identifies the precise place and current access, this remains historical information rather than a usable recommendation.
records.opening_notes: Old source mentions noon until evening before closure; no verified current schedule.

records.description: Limanakia A is the first of the rocky coves below Poseidonos Avenue on the coast between Vouliagmeni and Varkiza. The old cruising entry suggests approaching from the Limanakia A bus stop and descending on the rough trail towards the rocky shore rather than looking for a sandy beach. It describes encounters during the day and afternoon, and a December 2025 commenter called the area active into the evening, but there's no explicit recent firsthand encounter in that comment. Limanakia B is another cove farther along and should not automatically be merged with A, even though their descriptions overlap. Take footwear suitable for uneven rocks, avoid the water in poor conditions, and respect swimmers and other beachgoers. The exact crowd and dependable visiting times are still too uncertain for a verified recommendation.
blockers: Recent comment is a broad claim rather than dated firsthand encounter
Need corroboration specifically for Limanakia A versus B
Crowd and reliable best time unknown
records.address: Limanakia A cove, Poseidonos Avenue, Vouliagmeni–Varkiza coast
records.opening_notes: Archived suggestion daytime and afternoon, with a December 2025 opinion about evenings; no operator hours.

records.description: Calton Hill is one of Edinburgh's famous skyline viewpoints, with the monuments and paths above the city centre. It also appears in two older specialist cruising directories, but neither gives a readable firsthand encounter from the past year or even a reliably identified section of the hill. Some slopes are steep, heavily visited and subject to heritage and nature management. A conservation proposal for the Greenside hillside was still under consideration in 2026, not automatically a new restricted reserve. The hill is a sightseeing attraction first; don't interpret every quiet path as a cruising spot or presume safe access after dark. Without an exact area, recent visitor accounts, useful times or any indication of who attends, the directory entry is not ready to publish as a gay cruising recommendation.
records.tags: Historic Hill, Tourist Viewpoint, Historical Reports
records.opening_notes: Public heritage hill; paths and access restrictions vary. No reliable cruise timing.
